The eight ensemble and thematic arguments at this intake do not currently present a demonstrated incompatible claim about the same actor, act, recipient, narrative layer and time. This is an author audit finding, subject to independent root acceptance. It is not an aggregate R10 pass or authorization to revise the final synthesis.

The comparison also exposes why agreement must not be manufactured by reducing every document to the same thesis. An acquired form can be usable, an end owned, an action causally effective, a representation moving and a method still improperly scoped. These predicates have different objects. The effort study's distinctions among exertion, mastery, result, ownership, means and viability do not compete with the social-system study's distinction between receivability and accountable responsibility. The former asks what effort serves and can sustain; the latter asks how a field permits action and moves costs. The care study adds whose attachment supports an answerable relation. Authorship adds who selects and offers a likeness. Language adds who actually owns or hears each proposition. Removing those differences would weaken the analytical corpus even if it made the vocabulary uniform.

The positive argument is equally shared and equally differentiated. Learned presentation can make genuine curiosity possible. Chosen company, warmth, jokes, games, work and craft have value before a crisis and outside rescue. A recipient can make something of a flawed story which its authors did not fully control. Those goods do not need to be denied because a later test is unavailable. They also do not supply missing prior permission, full restitution, unlimited capacity, a livelihood or the dead person's standpoint. The audit preserves both sides rather than treating every good as an alibi or every defect as proof that no good occurred.

One conceptual tension remains useful: AO-E01's combination of self-inclusion, revisable attention and owned wish is an interpretation of a responsible authored offer.
